source.title: L0 is not a neutral hyperparameter

page_placements.theme: Fidelity and feature interpretability can diverge

record.tranche_reason: The post varies SAE L0 and a mixed-L0 training objective in a toy model with known features, and reports how these training choices affect feature recovery. This bears on the training-artifact component of V6, but it does not measure dark-matter residuals directly.
record.gate_note: The post reports feature-recovery outcomes for several L0 settings and a mixed-L0 objective, plus an MSE comparison. It does not measure linear predictability of SAE errors, error norms across SAE sizes or tokens, effects on model loss from replacing activations, or the function carried by an error term. The reported feature-recovery results are recorded only for V6; the post does not test V1–V5.
record.test_reason: The post measures how training L0 and a mixed-L0 objective affect feature recovery in a 20-feature toy model. It never measures SAE error or dark matter: no linear predictability of the residual, no error-norm scaling, no model-loss splicing, no error-term function, and no test of whether residual error shrinks with better training. Showing that a training hyperparameter changes which features are learned is a related but different construct from V6, which claims dark matter (the unexplained error) is a training artifact. The one MSE comparison (r3) shows a wrong-feature SAE reaching lower reconstruction error. That bears on feature quality, not on the origin or size of the residual. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that too-low L0 makes the SAE 'cheat': broken hedged latents give better MSE than the correct features. The authors frame this as feature hedging and argue there is a 'correct' L0 to find. The record's claim that the mixed-L0 loss works when the high-L0 loss is weighted enough matches the text (λ=20).
record.recipe_differences: Uses a synthetic correlated-feature toy model and varies Global BatchTopK SAE L0 and a mixed-L0 training loss; it does not test the original study's error-predictability or error-scaling measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature recovery and hedging vary with SAE L0 and with the mixed-loss coefficient λ.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 20-feature toy model, a BatchTopK SAE with L0 below the true L0 hedges (mixes f0 into other latents) and reaches lower MSE (0.42 vs 0.53) than the correct features cut to k=4. L0 above the true value gives degenerate latents. A mixed-L0 loss with λ=20 recovers the true features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature correctness depends on matching training L0 to the data's true L0; a wrong L0 yields wrong features, and too-low L0 is rewarded by MSE.

record.problems: The evidence is from one synthetic toy model with 20 features and 20 latents. Outcomes are described qualitatively, with no uncertainty estimates reported. It does not measure dark-matter residuals directly or test real language models.

untested.parts: All: no test of whether SAE error is linearly predictable from input activations.
All: no per-token error norms, no cross-size comparison, no scaling.
All: no splicing into a model and no random-error comparison.
All: no circuits or steering with or without the error term.

All: dark matter is never measured. Only feature recovery under varied L0 is measured, so there is no evidence on whether residual error is a training artifact or shrinks with better architectures or end-to-end training.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels attached V6 verdicts to feature-recovery rows. V6 concerns dark matter (residual error), which this post never measures, so all labels are removed. The toy model has no irreducible error, so dark matter cannot arise there in the original paper's sense. The post does not cite the original dark-matter paper.

versions.untested_parts: No measurement of whether SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
No per-token error-norm scaling, cross-size error comparison, context overlap, or test of whether error vanishes with scale.
No replacement of model activations with SAE reconstructions compared with random errors, and no model-loss test.
No decomposition of SAE error into linear and nonlinear parts, or test of further dictionary learning on those parts.
No test of circuits, steering, or other model behavior with versus without the SAE error term.

Tests the effect of L0 and a mixed-L0 objective on feature recovery in one toy model. Does not measure dark matter directly, establish that it mostly reflects training choices, or test shrinkage from better architectures or end-to-end training.

relation.reason: The post discusses related SAE training failures without testing residual predictability, scaling, functional effects, or the training-artifact explanation of dark matter.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure feature recovery and hedging under different L0 objectives. They neither test a dark-matter claim version nor use that finding as a tool.

source_check.notes: Reconstruction MSE is measured, but its comparison does not establish a dark-matter result. Perfect feature recovery is reported; zero reconstruction error at the matched L0 is not quantified.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Toy model with 20 features, Global BatchTopK SAE, varied L0 and mixed-L0 training
reader_labels.reason: Feature recovery changes substantially with the training L0, and the mixed-L0 objective recovers the true features at λ=20; these results support a training-choice contribution to SAE feature errors in this toy setting (r1–r11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The post measures learned-feature quality rather than dark-matter residuals and does not establish that dark matter mostly has a training-artifact origin or that it shrinks with improved architectures or end-to-end training (r1–r11).
